- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33) and forecast is trending up, lower the forecast by 3–5% to reflect mean reversion.  
- For 30-day horizons, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong downward momentum, reduce forecasted mean by 2–4% to account for lagged correction.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.33) and forecast is above recent 10-day average, apply a downward bias of 1–3% to avoid overconfidence.  
- If forecasted price exceeds true outcome by >5% in the first 5–7 days of the 30d window, adjust downward by 2–5% to correct for early overreaction.  
- For sentiment history with repeated high values (e.g., 1.00 for 3+ days), reduce forecasted volatility by 10–15% to avoid overestimating bullish momentum.
